title: Unique determination and generation of rank two single-qubit quantum channels
authors: Nina Kuklina, Vasilii Vasilenko, Boris Volkov, Alexander Pechen
abstract: An important problem in quantum technologies is the generation of a target evolution of an open quantum system. A core component of this task is the ability to determine whether the actual evolution of the system coincides with the target evolution. For the generation of unitary quantum channels in open quantum systems, it was shown by Goerz, Reich and Koch [New J. Phys. {\bf 16} 055012 (2014)] that for determining whether the actual evolution coincides with a desired unitary it is sufficient to compare their action on three special density matrices. In this work, we consider controlled generation and unique determination of non-unitary quantum channels in open quantum systems with particular emphasis on rank two single-qubit quantum channels. We prove that to uniquely determine such quantum channels it is sufficient to consider their action on only three suitably chosen density matrices. Based on this theoretical result, we numerically investigate generation of various non-unitary target single-qubit quantum channels in open quantum systems using coherent and incoherent controls.
summary: This paper theoretically establishes the minimal set of input states needed to uniquely identify a quantum channel, focusing on the challenging case of non-unitary, rank two single-qubit channels. The authors prove that only three carefully selected density matrices are sufficient for this unique determination. This result has direct implications for quantum process characterization and the design of quantum control protocols.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the minimal number of input quantum states required to uniquely determine an unknown, non-unitary quantum channel acting on an open system.
main_result: The authors prove that for rank two single-qubit quantum channels, it is sufficient to consider the channel's action on only three suitably chosen density matrices.
method: The work uses theoretical analysis involving the Choi matrix representation and the study of affine subspaces defined by the action of the channel on a set of input states.
model_or_system: The system involves open quantum systems modeled by single-qubit quantum channels ($	ext{Chan}(2, 2)$), which are represented by CPTP maps. The analysis focuses specifically on channels of rank two.
key_observables: The primary observables are the quantum channels themselves, characterized by their action on specific density matrices, and the resulting minimal required number of states ($k$).
important_parameters: The rank of the channel ($	ext{rank } \Phi$) and the number of input states ($k$) are key parameters. The analysis is restricted to single-qubit systems.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the ability to characterize the channel uniquely by its action on a finite set of states, which is proven to be true for the specific class of rank two channels.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures showing histograms of objective functional values for generating the phase damping channel using coherent and incoherent controls, and control patterns themselves.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general bounds on the number of required states (requiring $n^2$ states generally) to proving the specific, minimal result of $k=3$ for rank two single-qubit channels, followed by numerical investigation of channel generation.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical result on the distinguishability of quantum channels, which is crucial for quantum process tomography and quantum control theory in open systems.
